paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: : Linguistic and geographic trends over time in harmful language research. Notably, the number of datasets for the non-top five languages continues to be lower than all English ones, while since 2017 we see more and more datasets in languages other than English.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates how the number of harmful-language research datasets varies by year and by language category. The horizontal axis lists the categories as years in chronological order from 2012 through 2022 (labeled “Year”), and for each year multiple adjacent bars indicate different language groupings as defined in the legend. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^0\), \(10^1\), and \(10^2\) (spanning roughly 1 to 100 datasets). Bars are color-coded by the legend: English (blue), All other (orange), Arabic (green), Bengali (red), Spanish (purple), and Russian (brown), arranged as grouped (side-by-side) bars within each year rather than stacked. Visually, English (blue) appears in every year, with approximate values of about 2 (2012), 2 (2013), 3 (2014), 3 (2015), 10 (2016), ~25 (2017), ~35 (2018), ~45 (2019), ~80 (2020), ~90 (2021), and ~14 (2022). “All other” (orange) begins around 2016 at ~3, then is ~16 (2017), ~12 (2018), ~22 (2019), ~75 (2020), ~45 (2021), and ~18 (2022). Arabic (green) is shown from 2017 onward at approximately ~3 (2017), ~5 (2018), ~4 (2019), ~7 (2020), not visibly present in 2021, and ~3 (2022). Bengali (red) appears at approximately ~1 (2017), ~1 (2018), ~2 (2019), ~4 (2020), and ~13 (2021), with no visible red bar in 2022. Spanish (purple) appears at roughly ~4 (2017), ~4 (2019), ~10 (2020), and ~11 (2021), with no visible purple bar in 2018, 2022, or earlier years. Russian (brown) appears at about ~6 (2019), ~9 (2020), ~9 (2021), and ~1 (2022). The bars are not sorted by magnitude; they are organized by year, and there are no annotations or special visual emphasis beyond the legend and standard coloring.
